_comment: A multiple linear regression fitted from a named featureset. This is what a featureset is for: the warrant names nj_home_core@v1 rather than enumerating six columns, so the same selection can train another model, and two warrants differing only in their featureset are an honest A/B on data. The featureset fixes the columns; the warrant fixes the period.

operation.note: Ordinary least squares. T2 because the parameter object is inhabited by estimation rather than by training or calibration, and that class is derived from how P is inhabited rather than declared.

source.note: this warrant is the fit; the coefficients it produces come back as a parameter set naming this warrant, and a scoring warrant names that set

realisation.note: MAYA does not fit anything. It issues this and takes delivery of the result.

inputs.name: training_set
inputs.description: Six slots and a label, each pinned to an exact feature view version. Publishing a newer view version changes nothing here: rolling forward is a deliberate act that mints v2 and reports what moved.

outputs.description: Law L-W4: a fit must say where the parameters go. They come back to MAYA as a parameter set bound to this model version, this featureset version and this window — and cannot be run on until somebody other than whoever fitted them has approved.

assumptions: Residential sales in New Jersey only; the municipality dummies are NJ codes
Arm's length transactions; foreclosure and intra-family sales are excluded upstream
Log-linear in area, which is why the slot holds log_living_area and not the raw square footage
